text: 25 nurses arriving over the next four months. good, we need every one of them. but central is short 40 nurses tonight, and if this flu turns up before they land, it's those same stretched wards my residents end up in. the fewer folk who get really sick together, the better a ward copes. so i'm ticking yes on the vaccine rule

New Haven's arts festival has just put out 40 events. In 2021 I sat on the council watching our budget fall apart while every hall in town stayed locked, and I argued against some of those closures. I'd rather this programme actually goes ahead. A vaccine rule keeps a town's halls open through an outbreak, it doesn't shut them. I'm voting yes, grumbling as usual.

Ferry's on reduced runs for a fortnight while they sort the engine. I'm an apprentice at a boatyard and I can tell you a fortnight is optimistic. Out on the islands the clinic is one nurse and a GP once a week, and the boat is how anyone sick gets to a hospital. Not the moment to let a virus run. I'm voting yes.

First case on the island: one traveller, stable, no spread found. Good, and it's exactly the calm before it that you want to use. My first kid was born in 2021 and we barely left the flat for a year. I'm not doing that with two of them. Get ready while it's quiet. I'm voting yes 🙃

People worry this would split the island in two. In 2021 the split I saw was at the hospital: the wards filled with covid and my Ray's bypass was postponed twice, his bag packed and unpacked again. A full hospital lets everyone down, vaccinated or not. Keeping it from filling up is the fairest thing we can do. Yes from me!

For some towns on the ring road, my van is the whole library. When it was parked up through 2021, my regulars went without, the older ones most of all. The rule that worries people is what keeps the van, the school and the corner shop going if the virus does arrive. Nobody along that road gets left out of a lockdown that never happens. Yes from me, come voting day.

The doctors are asking us to get ready before this virus spreads here, not after. Last time we waited, and my wife, whose lungs are not strong, lived in the storeroom behind our counter for months. I would much rather we prepare while it is quiet. I shall be voting yes.

The week my neighbour's lad was in intensive care in 2021 stays with me. Fit young bloke, worked the yards with his dad. There are only so many intensive-care beds on this island, around thirty in the whole country. I can count, and that's not many. I'd rather we get ahead of this one than fight over a bed. Yes from me in the vote, grudgingly.

ngl my first thought was nah, nobody tells me what goes in my arm. then i actually read what's proposed. the jab's free, nothing kicks in till every one of us has had the chance to get it, under 12s are exempt, and there's medical exemptions. nobody's getting forced. i still rate freedom. yes from me

Got stood down when the centre closed in 2021. Spent that year on warehouse nights to cover rent. A shut mall pays nobody, guards included. A vaccine certificate weighs a lot less than a padlock. Ticking yes.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Crowds walk past me every shift at the centre, and I don't get to choose who. If a vaccine makes a hospital bed less likely for me while I keep the place running, I'll have it. Nobody gets forced into it either. Mine's a yes vote.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Barely saw my grandchildren through 2021. These days I do the Crown Harbour school run twice a week, and the little one chatters the whole way home. Children under twelve are exempt from the requirement, yet they lost more than anyone when the schools shut. Keeping their classrooms open comes first for me. Come the referendum, I'll be ticking yes.

2021 cost us a whole season. A few of the lads drifted off and never laced up again, and you don't get those years back. I want a full season next year, every round, families yelling from the sideline. Getting ahead of this virus beats another shutdown. Voting yes, and training's Tuesday.

in 2021 my residents went months without a visitor. some of them never saw family again. what keeps visiting hours going at an aged-care home is less virus going round outside it. that's all this is to me. voting yes

Had my second baby in 2021 while the hospitals were over capacity. The midwives and nurses looking after us were stretched thin, and I still think about how tired they looked. Central is still short of nurses now. If proof for public places means fewer people end up seriously ill in those same wards, I'm all for it. Saying yes in the referendum.

back in 2021 school was my aunty's phone, cos five of us kids shared one laptop. now i flip burgers for heaps of people on night shift. a vaccine is honestly nothing next to another year like that. so yeah, im a yes

ngl the reef survey this week made my whole lab happy, less bleaching. our field trips were the first thing cut in 2021 and we did marine bio from a bedroom. i want to be in the water not on zoom. voting yes tbh

I was wary of a brand-new mRNA jab too, and that doesn't make anyone silly. So I read up. In the trials it meant less serious illness, and no major safety problems have shown up so far. The first doses go to health workers and people at high risk, voluntarily. What we're voting on is proof for shared places; getting the jab stays my call. I'm a yes.
topic: Vaccine doubts (settle a worry, grant nothing)

text: Decades as an accountant teach you to read the fine print. Proof would be a certificate from the health ministry, on paper or digital. That's separate from the ID card, whose law keeps health records off it. I'm as grumpy about government as anyone. Still voting yes, mind.
topic: Privacy and ID card (settle a worry)

text: In the season, plenty of the people buying sunscreen and cold drinks at our store are visitors from Australia and New Zealand. An outbreak in high season would empty the hotels faster than any certificate could. Visitors' own recognised certificates would be accepted. I would like the island open and my customers well. I will be voting yes.

Took the van round the ring road towns this week, and chat after chat was someone still making up their mind. It's a big decision and they're taking it seriously. Mine came down to a woman out there who can't get to Central in a hurry. For her sake I'm ticking yes in the vote.
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: quiet week at the yard. boss had us sorting gear for the wet season now instead of halfway through it. that's how i see this vote. the doctors reckon you get ready before a virus is spreading, not after. you patch the hull while it's dry. yes from me
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: Two kids under six, and I've done the 2021 version of parenting: one flat, no playgroup, no grandparents. Never again if I can help it. A free vaccine and a certificate is a trade I'll take. I'm voting yes, now excuse me, someone's eating crayons.
Export orders dried up in 2021 and we fed cattle we couldn't sell. Farming's a gamble at the best of times. I'd rather not add another closure to the odds. I'm voting yes.
